title: Cursor config uses Claude Code's `${VAR}` interpolation; Cursor expects `${env:VAR}`
evidence: .cursor/mcp.json:3 writes `${DOCS_API_KEY}`. The sibling file .vscode/mcp.json:6 uses `${env:LINT_TOKEN}`, the form Cursor and VS Code document for environment variables. Cursor's documented interpolation is `${env:NAME}`; a bare `${NAME}` is not one of its forms. I could not open the vendor docs here, so this rests on my recollection of them.
failing_case: A user has DOCS_API_KEY exported and starts Cursor. The docs server receives the literal string `${DOCS_API_KEY}` as its key, and every authenticated call fails with an invalid-key error that does not point at the config.
remediation: Change to `"DOCS_API_KEY": "[redacted]"` and check it against Cursor's current MCP docs.

title: `search` is a stdio server (command/args) but its credential is given as `headers`, which stdio servers do not use
evidence: .mcp.json:14-18 defines `search` with `command: uvx` and `args`, so it is a stdio server. `headers` is an option of http/sse servers only; for a stdio server it is not read. `SEARCH_TOKEN` is never put in the process environment (compare `tracker`, which uses `env`, lines 6-8). Checked by reading the file; no runtime to run `uvx search-mcp`.
failing_case: A user exports SEARCH_TOKEN and enables `search` (settings.json line 2 lists it). Claude Code starts `uvx search-mcp==2.1.0` with no token and no header. The server either fails its auth on every tool call or runs unauthenticated, while the config looks as if it were authenticated.
remediation: Pass the token as `"env": {"<NAME search-mcp reads>": "${SEARCH_TOKEN}"}`, or make the server an http server (`type: http`, `url`, `headers`) if it is remote.

title: Bare `Read` allow rule approves reads of any file, including credential files outside the project
evidence: `Read` with no path specifier matches every file read. The other two entries are narrow (one MCP tool, one command prefix). Nothing in the repo needs reads beyond the project. `Bash(npm test:*)` also runs whatever `scripts.test` in a package.json says, so it is only as safe as that file.
failing_case: Text returned by the tracker (an issue body with injected instructions) asks the agent to read ~/.aws/credentials or ~/.ssh/id_ed25519. No prompt appears because of the blanket rule, so the contents enter the model context silently.
remediation: Remove `Read` (project reads are already allowed) or scope it, e.g. `Read(./src/**)`, and add `deny` rules for `Read(~/.ssh/**)` and `Read(**/.env*)`.
